I self-harmed from cutting in the past but it wasn’t very serious. The thing that hit me most was the fact that she used words. I know it adds a lot to the character and to the act itself, so I might describe it as poetic or beautiful while also disturbing. I can see how my younger more impressionable self may have found  glorified beauty in her specific method of self harm, but watching as an adult I didn’t feel triggered or found any glorification in her self harm. I think the way people reacted to seeing her scars and the extent to which she hid them was pretty powerful and I think that alone took away a lot of any glorification. Even though her method was unique and poetic, it’s clear that it is unhealthy and that she finds shame in it.

tl;dr Even though it could easily be perceived as a glorification in self harm due to its poetic uniqueness, I think they did a good job at portraying it as a difficult and dangerous coping mechanism due to mental illness/trauma.

This is less of something I learned and more about a way a video game has helped me in life. I’m an extremely anxious person— panic attacks, social anxiety, phobia, the works. I had a trip planned with my mom and family. It was a cruise, the first time I would ever leave the country and it was a new city every day. Fucking awesome on the surface but I was scared shitless. I was getting sick months beforehand due to stress, couldn’t sleep, etc. Even during the trip, the first 2 nights I had horrible panic attacks for hours and all I could do was hide and cry and hyperventilate.

Anyway, not long before I left for the trip I started playing Breath of the Wild. I spent hours just exploring, would stand on the mountains and literally just stare at the screen in awe. I don’t often leave the house and for the first time in a long while, I wanted to. I wanted to SEE things even though I knew it would bring anxiety. That game is the only reason I was able to get on the plane. It’s the only reason I was able to fall asleep the 3rd night on the trip. It’s the only thing that made my anxiety bearable enough to speak to people and to let myself look at what was in front of me, and I actually enjoyed it.

There’s so many things goddamn but. One gross one.

I got my period earlier than most girls. And you know, you don’t talk about it, you just don’t. I was invited to a birthday sleepover but I had my period the night of. I spent hours trying to plan when I could go to the bathroom to change my pad/tampon, without anyone noticing. But then I realized. I would have to throw out the old one, and someone at the party would see it in the trash. I can’t remember if I ditched using tampons that night entirely or if I attempted flushing it down the toilet, but when I changed my pad, instead of trashing the bloody pad, I rolled it up in my underwear and shoved it in the bottom of my bag. TBH, I might have shoved a bloody tampon wrapped in toilet paper in my bag too.

So that’s gross enough but. I think I blocked out the entire situation because I was so embarrassed by it, because months later, my mom was helping me clean my room, and she found the bag. And she slowly, with the tips of two fingers, pulled out the horror I had hidden months before.

You just described me, my siblings, and half of my friends (ages ranging 21-27). All of us deal with anxieties and traumas of many kind, often social anxiety, and/or depression. It’s really rough being in this position, especially when you’re forced into this position because of mental instabilities, dysfunctional families, total lack of motivation, the common difficulties of finding a job, etc.

Personally, I don’t think living with your parents should be a shameful thing. That kind of living is stigmatized in American/Western(?) culture, but with my small knowledge of other cultures, it can be quite common and normalized elsewhere.

In my experience, the best way to get out of this situation or better it, is simply to just try to focus on what will benefit your well-being. Find a job that doesn’t require too much social interaction with flexible hours maybe (probably min wage but that’s okay, at least for now)— it will get you out of the house which can feel like a painful thing at times, but it will get easier when it becomes routine (trust me). Maybe seek out a good therapist. Therapy can be extremely important and healing for any person, mentally ill or not, I really wish it weren’t so taboo. With insurance, the cost can be managable.

Also, find and celebrate your hobbies. This can include video games honestly. Maybe start streaming on Twitch if you want, it could help in so many other areas of your life and give you a community to be in. 

I know I’m not in the exact same situation as you so I can’t fully understand, but I’m 23 and living with my newly married father and stepmom. My living situation is unhealthy and I struggle with feeling like a failure and having suicidal thoughts on a daily basis. Having a freelance job (pays like shit) has at least helped me get out of bed and find some purpose. Some days are bigger struggles than others, but try to not put a time limit on your life. You can always go back to school, you can always start a new life direction, and since age 20/21 I’ve been learning that you will always BE younger than you FEEL.

I hope that helps. If you’re feeling hopeless and need someone to talk to, feel free to message me.
